transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I... I hope it's okay that I'm here. I don't want to take up too much of your time, but... I've been having a little trouble lately. It's probably nothing, really, just my imagination acting up, but... I keep hearing things. Like, voices. It's so silly, I know. But it sounds just as clear as if someone were standing right there in my little studio apartment. They say my name, and... and they tell me my work is being judged. Even when the house is completely quiet and I know nobody is there. I'm sorry, does that sound crazy? I just... I wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by telling you.

Alongside hearing these voices, have you noticed any big changes in your mood—like feeling extremely sad, hopeless, or losing interest in things, or on the other hand feeling unusually energetic, elated, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Oh... um, yes, actually. I hope it's alright to mention this, I don't want to make a big fuss. But a little while ago, I... well, I had this period where I just had so much energy. It was wonderful at first, really. I was barely sleeping, maybe just a few hours a night, but I didn't feel tired at all! I had all these grand plans, you see—combining my caregiving work with these big art projects. I thought I could change everything, make it all so beautiful. 

But... the thing is, even when I was feeling so incredibly energized and working on all those big plans, I was still... still hearing those voices in my studio. And I started getting this feeling that people were watching my work, judging it while I was doing it. Is... is it normal to feel so upbeat but still have those things happening at the same time? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just want to be helpful.

Do you ever hear those voices or feel that people are watching and judging your work during times when you're not feeling especially energetic or elated—like when your mood feels more normal or even low?

Well, um... yes. I hope it's not a bother to admit this, but... yes, they do stick around. Even when I'm not feeling all that bubbly and full of ideas. 

Like, after that really energetic time passed, and I went back to just... you know, sleeping my normal hours and feeling a bit more quiet? The voices didn't stop. They kept right on going for, oh, several weeks, I think. And I still had that awful feeling that people were tracking what I was doing and judging my work. 

I kept thinking maybe I was just tired or stressed from my caregiving job, you know? I try so hard to do a good job there, I didn't want to think something was really wrong with me. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Did you notice the voices or the feeling of being watched and judged starting before that period of high energy began, or did they first appear once you were already feeling so energized?

Oh... um, well, let me think. I don't want to get the timeline wrong and confuse you. But, yes, I... I think they actually started before that really energetic time. 

It's... it's a little embarrassing to admit how long it's been going on. I kept hoping it was just a passing thing, you know? Just me being a bit overly imaginative. But... well, to be honest, the voices and that awful feeling that people are watching and judging my work... it's been happening for about nine months now. 

I'm so sorry I let it go on for so long before coming in. I really thought I could just push through it and keep doing a good job at work. I hope you're not upset with me for waiting. Am I... am I giving you the right details? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.

Thinking back over these past nine months as a whole, how much of that total time would you say you were experiencing that period of high energy or any other mood changes, compared to the time you had the voices or feeling watched without any mood changes at all?

Oh, um... let me try to think about the whole picture. I really want to make sure I give you the right answer. 

I try so hard to just keep a smile on and push through, you know, for my clients. But... if I'm being completely honest about the whole nine months... I guess for most of that stretch, I was either all wound up with those big plans and getting hardly any sleep, just constantly doing things... or, well, I was sort of coming down from all that, but still not quite feeling back to my normal self yet. 

So the mood changes took up a really big chunk of that time alongside everything else. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm just complaining, I know other people have it much worse. I just want to be as helpful as I can. Am I doing okay with these questions?
